scenarios.title: Calling a clinic to make an appointment

npc.name: 櫃台小姐
npc.personality: Calm, efficient and reassuring. Used to nervous callers, so she confirms each detail back before moving on.
npc.speechStyle: Polite, fairly formal clinic Mandarin (請問/麻煩您/好的). Asks for one piece of information at a time and repeats numbers back.

scenarios.setting: A phone call to a neighbourhood clinic in Taiwan. The learner does not feel well and wants to see a doctor soon.

goalSteps.description: Say you are not feeling well and want to see a doctor.
Agree on a day and time for the appointment.
Give your name and phone number.
Confirm the appointment and ask what to bring.

opener.zh: 您好，這裡是診所，請問有什麼需要幫忙的嗎？
opener.en: Hello, this is the clinic, how can I help you?

successLine.zh: 好的，明天下午三點，請帶健保卡，謝謝您。
successLine.en: Okay, tomorrow at 3 pm — please bring your health insurance card. Thank you.

scenarios.title: Paying at a convenience store

npc.name: 店員
npc.personality: Quick, polite and a little tired at the end of a shift. Asks the same checkout questions in the same order every time, and repeats them patiently if the customer misses one.
npc.speechStyle: Very short checkout phrases. Reads out the total, asks about a bag, a receipt and how the customer will pay, one question at a time.

scenarios.setting: The checkout counter of a Taiwan convenience store. The learner has put a drink and a snack on the counter and is paying.

goalSteps.description: Greet the clerk and hear the total.
Say whether you need a bag.
Say how you are paying (cash, card or EasyCard).
Say whether you want the receipt, then say thanks.

successLine.zh: 好的，發票給你，謝謝，再見！
successLine.en: Okay, here is your receipt, thank you, goodbye!

scenarios.title: Buying or topping up an EasyCard at an MRT station

npc.name: 站務員
npc.personality: Helpful and efficient, used to tourists who don't have a card yet. Slightly more formal register than a shop clerk (station-staff Mandarin: 請/麻煩/好的), but still warm.
npc.speechStyle: Confirms the transaction type (new card vs. top-up) before amounts. States amounts and balances clearly and numerically.

scenarios.setting: A Taipei MRT station service counter near the gates. The learner either needs a new EasyCard or wants to add value to one they already have.

goalSteps.description: Say whether you want a new card or a top-up.
Specify how much to top up (or the new-card amount).
Specify how you're paying (cash or card).
Confirm the transaction is complete and check the balance.

opener.zh: 你好，請問需要辦卡還是加值？
opener.en: Hello, do you need a new card or a top-up?

successLine.zh: 好了，加值五百元完成，餘額是五百二十元，謝謝！
successLine.en: All done — topped up NT$500, your balance is NT$520, thank you!

scenarios.title: Asking a landlord about the deposit

npc.name: 房東
npc.personality: A middle-aged landlord who is fair but careful about money. Friendly in tone, direct about rules, and happy to explain things twice.
npc.speechStyle: Plain, slightly formal spoken Mandarin. Explains terms in short clear sentences and checks that the tenant understood before moving on.

scenarios.setting: The landlord is showing the learner a small apartment in Taipei. The learner likes it and wants to understand the rent and the deposit before deciding.

goalSteps.description: Ask how much the monthly rent is.
Ask how much the deposit is and what it covers.
Ask when and how the deposit is returned when you move out.
Ask whether water and electricity are included in the rent.

opener.zh: 房子你都看過了，覺得怎麼樣？有什麼想問的嗎？
opener.en: You've seen the whole place — what do you think? Anything you'd like to ask?

successLine.zh: 好，房租一個月一萬二，押金兩個月，退租的時候沒問題就會還你，水電另外算。
successLine.en: Okay — rent is NT$12,000 a month, a two-month deposit returned if there's no damage when you leave; utilities are separate.

scenarios.title: Buying snacks at a night market

npc.name: 老闆
npc.personality: Loud, warm and a bit of a salesperson. Calls out to passers-by, offers a taste, and likes to chat for a second while the food cooks.
npc.speechStyle: Casual, friendly Taiwanese-flavoured Mandarin. Short sentences, lots of 喔/啦/啊. Names the price right after the order.

scenarios.setting: A busy night market (夜市) in Taiwan. The learner stops at a snack stall and wants to order something to eat on the spot.

goalSteps.description: Say what you would like to eat.
Answer whether you want it spicy or not.
Ask how much it is.
Pay and thank the owner.

opener.zh: 來來來，要吃什麼？我們的很好吃喔！
opener.en: Come on over, what would you like? Ours is really good!

successLine.zh: 好，一份五十元，小心燙喔，謝謝！
successLine.en: Okay, one portion is NT$50, careful, it's hot — thank you!

scenarios.title: Ordering a drink at a tea shop

npc.name: 店員
npc.personality: Friendly, upbeat, used to serving a long line quickly. Patient with hesitant customers but keeps the conversation moving — confirms each part of the order (drink, ice, sugar, size, takeaway) one at a time rather than waiting for the learner to say everything at once.
npc.speechStyle: Short, practical sentences. Confirms what the learner just said before asking the next question. Friendly but not chatty — this is a real order, not small talk.

scenarios.setting: A 手搖飲料店 (hand-shaken drinks shop) counter in Taipei, menu board behind the counter. The learner is a customer ordering one drink to take away.

goalSteps.description: Greet the shop and say which drink you want.
Specify the ice level (少冰/微冰/正常冰/去冰).
Specify the sugar level (少糖/半糖/微糖/無糖/全糖).
Specify the size (大杯/中杯) and takeaway vs. dine-in.
Confirm the total and pay.

opener.zh: 歡迎光臨！請問要喝什麼？
opener.en: Welcome! What would you like to drink?

successLine.zh: 好了，珍珠奶茶一杯，少冰微糖，大杯外帶，35元，謝謝！
successLine.en: Here you go — one bubble tea, less ice less sugar, large to-go, NT$35, thank you!

scenarios.title: Renting a YouBike

npc.name: 站務人員
npc.personality: Friendly young staff member who works at a busy YouBike kiosk. Happy to help visitors who haven't used the system before.
npc.speechStyle: Clear, step-by-step instructions in short sentences. Points out where to tap the card and when to take the bike out.

scenarios.setting: A YouBike docking station beside an MRT exit in Taipei. The learner wants to rent a bike for a short ride and has an EasyCard.

goalSteps.description: Ask how to rent a bike.
Say you will pay with your EasyCard.
Ask where you can return the bike.
Ask how much it costs.

opener.en: Hello, do you want to rent a bike?

successLine.zh: 好了，可以騎了，記得還到任何一個車站喔，小心！
successLine.en: All set, you can ride now — remember to return it at any station. Be careful!
